examples.solution_text:
$\angle ABC=180(7-2)^{\circ}\div7$ (interior angle of a regular heptagon)
$AB=BC$, so $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles (equal sides of a regular polygon)
$\angle BCA=(180^{\circ}-180(7-2)^{\circ}\div7)\div2$ (equal base angles and triangle angle sum)
$\angle BCA=25.71^{\circ}$ (to two decimal places)

examples.question_text: A regular pentagon and a regular octagon lie outside each other and share one complete side. Find the angle in the gap between their other sides at an endpoint of the shared side.
examples.solution_text:
$I_5=180(5-2)^{\circ}\div5=108^{\circ}$ (interior angle of a regular pentagon)
$I_8=180(8-2)^{\circ}\div8=135^{\circ}$ (interior angle of a regular octagon)
$g+108^{\circ}+135^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$ (angles at a point)
$g=117^{\circ}$

examples.question_text: Four interior angles of a pentagon are $90^{\circ}$, $85^{\circ}$, $165^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. Find the fifth interior angle $a$.
A concave pentagon has four interior angles of $90^{\circ}$, $55^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $105^{\circ}$. Find its reflex interior angle $a$.
A pentagon has interior angles $90^{\circ}$, $105^{\circ}$, $95^{\circ}$, $x^{\circ}$ and $x^{\circ}$. Find $x$.
In convex pentagon $ABCDE$, the exterior angles at $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $75^{\circ}$, $40^{\circ}$, $85^{\circ}$ and $65^{\circ}$. Find the exterior and interior angles at $E$.
examples.solution_text:
$75^{\circ}+40^{\circ}+85^{\circ}+65^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$ (exterior angle sum)
$265^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$
$E=95^{\circ}$
$I+95^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)
$I=85^{\circ}$

$\angle DBC=30^{\circ}$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle BDC$, since $BD=DC$)
$\angle BDC=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-30^{\circ}=120^{\circ}$ (triangle angle sum)
$\angle ADB=180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$ (angles on straight line $ADC$)
$\angle ABD=60^{\circ}$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABD$, since $AB=AD$)
$\angle BAD=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$ (triangle angle sum)

examples.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $(4a+10)^{\circ}$, $(3a+24)^{\circ}$ and $(4a-8)^{\circ}$. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}(4a+10)+(3a+24)+(4a-8)&=180\\11a+26&=180\\11a&=154\\a&=14\end{aligned}$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}4a+10&=66\\3a+24&=66\\4a-8&=48\end{aligned}$
Two angles are $66^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.

examples.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $(4a+12)^{\circ}$, $(3a+26)^{\circ}$ and $(4a-12)^{\circ}$. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}(4a+12)+(3a+26)+(4a-12)&=180\\11a+26&=180\\11a&=154\\a&=14\end{aligned}$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}4a+12&=68\\3a+26&=68\\4a-12&=44\end{aligned}$
Two angles are $68^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.

examples.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $x$, $y$ and $z$. Given $x+y=3z$, find $z$.

examples.solution_text:
$\angle AOB=360^{\circ}\div10=36^{\circ}$ (equal angles at the centre of a regular decagon)
$r+36^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$ (angles at a point)
$r=324^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC=180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$ (angles on straight line $ABD$)
$\angle BAC=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=75^{\circ}$ (triangle angle sum)

examples.question_text: In convex pentagon $ABCDE$, the interior angles at $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $90^{\circ}$, $145^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. Side $EA$ is extended beyond $A$, making an exterior angle of $60^{\circ}$ with $AB$. Find the interior angles at $A$ and $E$.
examples.solution_text:
$\angle EAB=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=120^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)
$S=180(5-2)^{\circ}=540^{\circ}$ (interior angle sum of a pentagon)
$\begin{aligned}120^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+145^{\circ}+100^{\circ}+\angle DEA&=540^{\circ}\\455^{\circ}+\angle DEA&=540^{\circ}\\\angle DEA&=85^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The source's Problems Q7 uses equal central angles followed by angles at a point. For the decagon, the smaller central angle is 360° ÷ 10 = 36°, so the reflex angle is 360° − 36° = 324°. The rays have directions 90° and 54°; the arc from 54° to −270° traces the required 324° reflex angle. Only O's label placement changed; vertices, rays, arc, givens and solution are preserved.
